subject: Private vs Dedicated: SSO/KMS/Log retention follow-up
raw_messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@privatelifthealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Private vs Dedicated: SSO/KMS/Log retention follow-up

Hi Ava — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Summary of customer constraints (as discussed)
- SSO: Okta SAML 2.0, IdP-initiated required; SCIM for user provisioning preferred but not mandatory in initial phase.
- Keys: Customer requires BYOK; keys must be controlled via their AWS KMS backed by an HSM (they may require a customer-managed HSM appliance for highest assurance).
- Logs: Full request/response audit logs; retained for up to 7 years; exportable to customer SIEM (pref: syslog or S3 with lifecycle rules).

Preliminary alignment from Redwood side
- Hosted API: easiest for time-to-value but does not meet BYOK/HSM and long on-prem log retention needs without Private controls.
- Dedicated capacity: can meet many isolation and export needs; BYOK support possible if customer-managed KMS is allowed and we can configure network connectivity to reach KMS endpoints.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): strongest match for HSM/BYOK and long-term log retention in customer-controlled systems.

Open questions / actions for Privatelift (what we need to confirm)
1) Exact KMS model: AWS KMS CMK with external key material? Or an on-prem HSM that must be reachable within customer network?
2) Where do you want logs to live initially (S3 vs on-prem ELK/SIEM)? Do you have an S3 bucket/account we can write to, or do you require a push via syslog/forwarder?
3) Network constraints: are egress rules strict (no outbound to internet) or can we peering with a VPC / private endpoint?
4) Procurement timeline and PO contact (cc procurement).

Recommended next steps
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineering team (Priyom) to map KMS/HSM options and network design (30–45 min).
- Share SOC 2 and audit artifacts (we will provide SOC 2 Type II and an architecture whitepaper).
- Rough cost delta: we will provide a Dedicated vs Private estimate after the tech deep-dive.

Attachments: Privatelift_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (draft SLA, includes key-ownership clause stub), redwood-deploy-checklist.xlsx (technical info we need from you).

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

--

From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@privatelifthealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@privatelifthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 16:18:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Private vs Dedicated: SSO/KMS/Log retention follow-up

Thanks Olga — really helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- We are leaning strongly toward a Private deployment because our compliance team insists that the private keys never leave our HSM and that audit logs are ingested into our on-prem ELK cluster.
- For KMS: we currently use an on-prem HSM that exposes a KMIP endpoint and also maintain multi-tenant AWS KMS with imported key material for certain workloads. Ideally we want an architecture where calls to the model never expose plaintext tokens outside our control.
- Logs: we need 7-year retention and must be able to demonstrate chain-of-custody for access. Export to S3 is OK as an interim, but long-term they want logs in our ELK.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports KMIP/HSM-backed BYOK in a Private deployment? If Private is the only viable option, please note that our procurement timeline is tight — we need a partner with a clear onboarding plan (network steps, hardening checklist, sign-off gating).

I'll loop in procurement as requested. My availability for the deep-dive: Wed 2027-07-14 between 10:00–12:00 PT.

Best,
Ava Reynolds
Head of Cloud Security | Privatelift Health
ava.reynolds@privatelifthealth.com
--

On Mon, Jul 12, 2027 at 18:02 Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ava / Olga / Neha — thanks for the context. Quick technical readout based on our options:
> 
> 1) Private (VPC / on-prem install) — best fit
>    - Pros: Full control for customer's HSM (KMIP or direct HSM appliance), private control plane, ability to install an on-prem log forwarder that writes to ELK with customer retention policies.
>    - Cons: Longer lead time (we need network onboarding, possible air-gapped install work), more operational support from both sides during onboarding.
> 
> 2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — possible compromise
>    - Pros: Faster to provision than full on-prem; can be configured to use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS CMK) if we can reach the KMS endpoint from our Dedicated nodes. We can also ship encrypted logs to a customer S3 bucket or set up secure push to your SIEM.
>    - Cons: If your requirement is a physical HSM that never exposes keys off-prem, Dedicated may not be sufficient unless we can colocate an HSM or broker key operations inside customer network.
> 
> Technical questions / items to confirm before the deep-dive call:
> - KMIP support: do you need KMIP directly or will an AWS KMS CMK with imported material satisfy compliance? If KMIP is mandatory, Private/on-prem is the recommended route.
> - Network model: can you provide a small diagram or list of required ports, CIDRs for peering, and whether private endpoints are acceptable?
> - SIEM/export: preferred method to ship logs (S3 write role vs syslog agent).
> 
> We can prepare a short runbook and a checklist for the deep-dive that covers key-wrap, HSM integration patterns, and network steps. I can host the technical call on Wed 2027-07-14 at 10:30 PT if that works for the Privatelift team.
> 
> Thanks,
> Priyom Das
> Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
> priyom.das@redwood.com
> --
>

From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@privatelifthealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@privatelifthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private vs Dedicated: SSO/KMS/Log retention follow-up

10:30 PT on Wed 7/14 works for me. Procurement will need an early look at the commercial delta between Dedicated and Private (ballpark %) and a proposed contract language for key ownership and data custody.

Also please confirm which SOC and audit artifacts you'll provide prior to the call so our compliance team can review.

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Regards,
Ava
